report:
### Conclusion
Contrary to your initial assumption, clinical evidence shows that the answer is **yes**: treatment with cortisone-like drugs, such as dexamethasone, significantly increases survival rates and reduces mortality among critically ill COVID-19 patients.

### Key Evidence

* **Reduction in Mortality Rates:** Data from clinical studies, including the landmark RECOVERY trial, demonstrated that dexamethasone reduced mortality by approximately one-third in the most severely ill hospitalized COVID-19 patients requiring mechanical ventilation or oxygen therapy (https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/wellness/story/demand-dexamethasone-soars-promising-findings-uk-71476859).
* **Global Health Guidelines:** The World Health Organization (WHO) issued a strong recommendation supporting systemic corticosteroid therapy for severe and critical COVID-19, based on clinical trial evidence showing clear survival benefits (https://www.who.int/news-room/feature-stories/detail/who-updates-clinical-care-guidance-with-corticosteroid-recommendations).
* **Standard of Care:** Medical guidance from public health agencies established dexamethasone as a standard of care for severe and ventilated COVID-19 cases due to its proven effectiveness in reducing fatal outcomes (https://www.healio.com/news/infectious-disease/20200709/fauci-covid19-was-id-physicians-worst-nightmare-warns-of-potential-airborne-spread).
* **Therapeutic Mechanism:** Critical COVID-19 triggers severe systemic inflammation and acute lung injury. Corticosteroids function as potent immunomodulators that calm this hyper-inflammatory immune response, thereby improving clinical outcomes and survival (https://www.pharmacist.com/DesktopModules/EasyDNNNews/DocumentDownload.ashx?portalid=0&moduleid=3675&articleid=2898&documentid=1160).
